correctness.rationale: For every integer a≥4 the 12 listed maximal cones have unimodular determinants and exactly 18 two-cone walls. Independently computed each symbolic primitive wall relation using SymPy matrix inverses with a symbolic integer parameter; all 18 anticanonical degrees agree with the source table: constants 2,-1,2,3,2,3,-1,1,2,2,-2,2 and affine terms a+2,1-a,a+1,3-a,a+1,1-a, with none zero for a≥4. Ray-seven star is the fan with five rays (1,1),(1,0),(0,-1),(-1,0),(0,1), hence Bl_p(P1×P1). The classes F1,F2,E form a Picard basis; boundary degree data (2,1,3) imply (-K)|S≡F1+2F2−3E. A general (1,1) curve through p is smooth irreducible rational, has strict transform F1+F2−E, is non-toric, and intersects L by 1+2−3=0. The quoted complete-curve tensor-generation criterion then proves non-generation. For every m≥1, sections of O(mL) are (m,2m)-biforms vanishing order≥3m at p, leaving just s^m t^{2m}; -mL has no sections after push-forward. This analytically justifies the invariant-surface obstruction beyond finite checks. The non-projectivity is established by the original Fujino–Sato primitive relation argument at b=2 and a≠0. Check relies on published tensor-generation criterion and fan classification, not re-proved here.

value.rationale: The explicit Question 6.6 about a natural non-projective four-parameter toric family motivates exactly this obstruction classification. The theorem gives an infinite counterfamily to invariant-(-1,-1)-curve-only tests, despite all 18 invariant curve canonical degrees being nonzero; the blowup-surface class and non-invariant rational curve explain the obstruction geometrically, not by an arbitrary isolated negative case.
